note: Shared definition for ffmpeg-encoded fixtures (generate-video-fixtures.py) and browser-encoded fixtures (recorder.html). Square waves: state = floor(t * 2 * hz) mod 2 at frame time t = n / fps, state 0 shows a, state 1 shows b. Moving regions start at x = -w and advance speed CSS px/s, wrapping after leaving the frame.

code.note: 12-bit Gray code of the source frame index, MSB first, in a low-contrast band. RGB 120 vs 132 is a relative-luminance change of about 0.043, below the 0.10 general-flash threshold, so the strip itself is not a flash.

fixtures.reference: 4 Hz but delta Y about 0.028, below the 0.10 threshold: no general flashes. Visible low-contrast flicker; not a seizure-safety claim.
Smooth low-contrast motion (delta Y about 0.068). No flashes. Exercises real frame rates without flashing.
Full-field black/white, 2 flashes per second: frequency-branch pass.
3 flashes per second: boundary pass (not more than three).
4 flashes per second over a large area: general-flash failure at reference geometry.
Saturated red/cyan at 4 Hz: general and red-flash failure.
32 x 32 source-pixel square at 10 Hz. Frequency candidates expected; area pass only if displayed small enough at reference geometry.
320 x 240 source-pixel region at 4 Hz. Failure when displayed above the reference area.

variants.reference: Source frames with n mod 7 == 3 removed; remaining timestamps keep source times (variable frame rate).
Source frames with n mod 5 == 4 replaced by the previous frame (duplicate frame code); constant frame rate.
